tasks.short: Take orders at the counter, enter them in the till, answer allergen questions, take payment and count the drawer.

steps.what: Cook greets customers and takes food and drink orders at the counter
Cook keys the order into the till
Cook answers questions about allergens and ingredients
Customer orders and pays by card at the kiosk or in the app
Customer pays by card or cash
Cook receives payment, gives change and hands over the receipt
Cook counts the cash drawer at the end of the shift

tasks.design: Self-order kiosks and app ordering linked to the {OTHER} point-of-sale till send orders straight to the kitchen screen with card payment, so the cook takes counter orders only for guests who prefer it. Allergen information per item comes from the recipe records and shows on the kiosk and a counter card; the cook still answers questions in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every order went through a person at the counter, and cash was the default.
tasks.enabler_now: Self-order kiosks, app ordering and card payment linked to the till are common in fast food.
tasks.still_hard: Some guests need help or want to talk; allergen data must be right because the operator stays responsible.
tasks.human_edge: A friendly word and quick help for a guest who is unsure, in a hurry or worried about an allergy.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less time at the till and more at the grill.

reach.task: Serve guests at the counter during rush hours
reach.learn: Whether kiosks shorten queues or move them to the pick-up point.

evidence.claim: Self-order kiosks and app ordering linked to the till are widely used in fast food.
Allergen information is mandatory for non-prepacked food, and the operator stays responsible for its accuracy.
In 2023 the food authority inspected 6,548 businesses; 51.8% of hospitality businesses fell short on allergen information.

assumptions: Scenario: about half of guests switch to kiosk or app; the rest still order at the counter.
Input contract: menu items, prices and allergen data per item kept by the restaurant manager in the till and recipe records; fallback is counter ordering.

Ordering time moves to customers (s1k, share 1) and is outside the cook's savings. s1, s2 and s5 keep 50 because about half of guests still order and pay at the counter; s3 keeps 70 because allergen information is shown and questions remain; s6 keeps 85 because the drawer is still counted, with less cash in it.
Kiosk hardware is a purchase decision by the franchise or owner.
unknowns: Share of guests who would use kiosks at this location.
research_questions: Do kiosks change average order value or queue time?

incremental.description: Cook helps guests who get stuck at the kiosk.
Cook refills kiosk paper and cleans screens.
Restaurant manager keeps kiosk menu, prices and allergen data current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about a quarter of guests switch, because most are regulars who prefer the counter or pay cash (21.4); high: about half switch as assumed (40.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count stock after closing, estimate needs, place the order with the distributor, receive and check the delivery, record temperatures and put away.

steps.what: Cook counts frozen, chilled and dry stock after closing
Cook estimates what is needed for the coming days from experience
Cook checks the final order before it goes: lines, quantities, delivery date and the distributor
Cook sends the supply order to the distributor: typed line by line into the portal today; after the change one send of the checked order, typing only items missing from the article list
Cook takes delivery of supplies and checks quantities and temperatures
Cook writes delivery temperatures on the paper food safety list
Cook puts stock away first in, first out

tasks.design: The cook counts on a tablet in storage order in the stock module of the {OTHER} point-of-sale till, which proposes an order from par levels, recent sales and planned promotions; the cook checks the final order and sends it to the distributor's {PARTNER_PORTAL} without retyping. A food safety app ({OTHER}) with a probe records delivery temperatures and warns when one is out of range.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts and orders were on paper and retyped into the portal, and temperatures were written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Till stock modules propose orders from sales, distributors take electronic orders, and food safety apps record measurements and warn on missed ones.
tasks.still_hard: Counting stays physical; promotions and weather swing demand beyond history.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that the local fair next week will double burger sales and spotting a thawed box at delivery.

ambition.what: Orders placed against expected sales at every delivery, so less product expires in the freezer.

tasks.altitude: The cook confirms orders instead of building them; spending limits stay with the manager.

reach.learn: Whether proposed orders bring actual use closer to theoretical use.

evidence.claim: A food safety registration app warns on missed measurements and offers temperature monitoring.
A recipe tool links recipes to supplier prices so costs follow price changes.
Food businesses must keep food safety records in proportion to their size and show them to the authority.
An approved hygiene code can replace a business's own food safety plan.

assumptions: Boundary: from the closing count to stock put away; invoice payment is outside.

Input contract: par levels and recipes per menu item set by the restaurant manager in the till; promotions entered by the manager; temperature limits from the hygiene code; fallback is paper count and typing.
The main distributor takes portal orders.

Manager time is outside the cook's savings. Putting away and the order check keep their full time; s1 keeps 85 because counting in storage order saves walking and the count stays; s2 keeps 40 for reviewing the proposal; s4 keeps 85 because the probe records temperatures and checking stays; s5 keeps 30 for reading warnings.
unknowns: Whether the till has a stock module.
How often deliveries come per week.
research_questions: Does expired stock fall after orders follow expected sales?

already_counted.description: Cook reviews the proposed order against known events.
Cook checks the order lines before they are sent.

incremental.description: Cook handles items missing from the distributor's article list.
Restaurant manager keeps par levels and recipes current.

approvals.approved_version: The supply order with lines, quantities and delivery date exactly as checked by the cook in s3c, sent once to the distributor's portal; edits after the check need a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: irregular events make the proposal unreliable, so most needs are still estimated by hand (25.8); high: steady trade where the proposal holds (31.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree the day's plan with the manager, work out pre-cook amounts per hour, plan equipment use, time cooking during service and log waste.

steps.what: Shift manager briefs the cook on promotions and expected rush hours
Cook works out how much to pre-cook per hour from experience
Cook plans fryer, grill and oven use and cleaning times on a whiteboard
Cook coordinates cooking times during service from the order screen and holding cabinet
Cook adjusts with the manager when a rush or breakdown happens
Cook notes food thrown away after holding time on a paper waste sheet

tasks.design: A cook-ahead chart per 15 minutes is computed from till sales history for the same day and time, adjusted for promotions the manager enters in the {OTHER} point-of-sale till, and an equipment schedule fills fryer, grill and oven slots and cleaning times from it. Holding timers on the kitchen screen let the cook log discarded items with one tap, so waste is counted per item without paper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pre-cook amounts came from memory, and waste sheets were filled in at the end of the shift, if at all.
tasks.enabler_now: Tills keep sales per item per quarter hour, and kitchen screens support holding timers and waste logging.
tasks.still_hard: Rushes do not follow history precisely; the cook must still watch the cabinet and the queue.
tasks.human_edge: Reading the queue and the car park and starting the next batch before the screen asks.

ambition.what: Cook-ahead amounts adjusted every quarter hour, not once per shift.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; planning starts from a computed chart.

reach.learn: Whether the same sales curve helps set crew levels.

evidence.claim: A food waste system weighs and identifies each discard and forecasts production per service.
A contract caterer cut food waste by 44% with automatic waste tracking; baseline and period not given (vendor claim).
A waste tool that logs who did what observes staff behaviour and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift plan to waste logged; ordering supplies is outside.

Input contract: sales per item per quarter hour from the till; promotions entered by the shift manager; holding times per item set by the franchise standards; fallback is the whiteboard and paper waste sheet.
Waste is logged per item, not per person.
Shift manager time is outside the cook's savings.
unknowns: Whether the kitchen screen supports holding timers.
How much food is discarded per day today.
research_questions: Does a quarter-hour cook-ahead chart cut discarded food without longer waits?

already_counted.description: Cook adjusts the computed cook-ahead chart for what they see.

incremental.description: Cook reports charts that miss rushes.
Shift manager keeps promotions and holding times current in the till.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small outlet with steady trade already pre-cooks by habit, so the chart and schedule save little (16.4); high: busy outlets where the chart replaces the estimate (27.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fast food cook keeps cooking, timing and guest contact; order taking, ordering and paper logs shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking proposed orders and cook-ahead charts
role.ambitious_version: A cook who spends the shift at the grill, with orders, stock and waste handled through the till.
